fields.source_title: Human Rights Forum — Suspend Environmental Clearances to Hyperscale Data Parks
fields.summary: The Human Rights Forum asked that the environmental clearances granted on 18 April 2026 to the Tarluvada and Rambilli data-centre parks be suspended and reclassified, arguing that the projects are energy- and water-intensive and need full scrutiny.

records.verbatim: Clearances (ECs) granted on 18 April 2026 by the State Environment Impact Assessment Authority (SEIAA)
records.notes: Probe HIT on the date and authority clause. Event is the clearance date. Records the NGO position. Adds the Rambilli park, whose project record is not yet in the seed. Single_source: true unless a second outlet is added.
Lead only. Reported as Nxtra's largest campus on 40 acres (secondary source, undated). Do not ship until a primary page or filing is probed.

leads: Visakhapatnam / Tarluvada (in-google-visakhapatnam): Guardian reports (via TheNextWeb, unverified) that AP clearance covers 2.51 GW against 1 GW announced, cleared in nine days with no public hearing; 520 families lost land granted about 20 years earlier; Dalit farmers say promised plots and jobs have not arrived. Fetch the Guardian article directly and probe before filing.

Visakhapatnam litigation: Andhra Pradesh High Court PIL by Bolisetty Satyanarayana (Jal Biradari) over about 160 acres of temple-linked land, the SEIAA Category B2 clearance, and a site-distance error (850 km recorded vs 0.86 km). Court allowed the developer to proceed at its own risk. Dates conflict across outlets; pull the court order or Deccan Chronicle / The News Minute reports with dates.

Visakhapatnam water: government says the city supplies 410 MLD against 480 MLD need; Green Visakha and Jal Biradari march and beach protests planned. Needs a dated primary (AP government or Hindu / Hans India) before a response record.

Tarluvada forest status: activists say about 90% of Tarluvada is notified forest, and Mongabay says the EC does not state a water source. Verify against the forest diversion record before use. The forest-reserve point is attributed to the Rambilli site in one report.

Thane Balkum (in-amazon-thane-balkum): Amazon statement, reported 9 Jul 2026 by Free Press Journal, that the facility 'will not draw potable water for cooling' and uses a dedicated substation. Reported paraphrase, not a verbatim quote. Could be recorded as a company response once Amazon's own page is found. Protest coverage also cites about 190 DG sets and heat concerns; an MP (Naresh Mhaske) objected.
Thane: Maharashtra Green Integrated Data Centre Parks plan (three 500 MW parks, Mumbai and Navi Mumbai) is a state policy lead. Verify against the official notification.

Mekagunda, Hyderabad (Microsoft): residents' High Court petition filed July 2023 alleging land encroachment and industrial waste dumping into Tungakunta lake. DCD article returned 403 to probe. Needs a second source and a 2026 status check.

Amazon Taloja / Navi Mumbai: reported $429.8m, 49-acre campus, 473 MW total (secondary, undated). Amazon's $35bn India pledge (Dec 2025) is unreconciled against state figures. Amazon Hyderabad Bharat Future City: INR 60,000 crore pledge; 220 acres allotted; no MW. Needs AWS or state primary.

CtrlS (company, not a project lead): CPP Investments commitment up to INR 7,000 crore (June 2026), verified as the wire-release headline only. CtrlS also cites INR 4,000 crore direct / 500 direct jobs for its Chennai Datacenter Park (date unclear). Needs CtrlS primary page.
Yotta: no campus MW or investment figure found in search. Yotta NM1 Navi Mumbai listed by Baxtel only. Needs Yotta primary.

Sify, NTT India: not researched beyond search mentions. OpenAI reportedly in talks for at least 1 GW in India with Yotta, CtrlS, Sify and E2E (Bloomberg/ET via secondary, 2025). No confirmed deal found.

Telangana state policy: 2016 framework is still cited; CII (16 Oct 2026) proposes Data Center Policy 2.0 with water benchmarks favouring treated wastewater; NITI Aayog asks for a 20-30 year catchment water balance. Needs the official NITI Aayog or CII document (both unverified here).
Telangana: Aloor 1,500-acre data centre city in preparation; CM asked for a water, electricity and connectivity report. Verify against the Telangana government release.

Tamil Nadu Data Centre Policy 2021 (secondary coverage): incentives conditional on at least 30% renewable energy supply and investment above INR 500 crore; state to ensure uninterrupted water supply for cooling; policy window Apr 2021 to Mar 2026 may have lapsed. Official G.O. not fetched.

Maharashtra IT/ITeS Policy 2023 (secondary): stamp-duty exemptions and INR 1/unit power subsidy for 5 years; data centres treated as essential service. No community-facing conditions found. Official resolution not fetched.
Andhra Pradesh Data Centre Policy 4.0 (secondary): target 6 GW; incentives reported near INR 22,000 crore. No conditions found; needs the official G.O.
Chennai water: no resident objection found for Sify, CtrlS or Yotta sites in Tamil Nadu. Coverage is general. Searches returned none; treat as an absence, not evidence of none.
